entry.title: Abell 2029 Press Release
entry.content:
Abell 2029: In the News

The last project that I worked on for my PhD dissertation focused on the galaxy cluster Abell 2029. Using the deepest X-ray observations ever taken of this cluster with NASA’s Chandra X-Ray Observatory, we found clear evidence that Abell 2029 — long considered the “most relaxed cluster in the universe” — is still recovering from a collision with a smaller cluster about 4 billion years ago. We found a sloshing spiral, a shock front, and a couple of other fun features we nicknamed the “bay” and the “splash.” Turns out even the calmest-looking corners of the universe have a past.

I submitted our findings to the Astophysical Journal and our work was published on 12/31/2025. NASA’s Chandra Observatory put out a press release on May 12th, and since then, the story has been picked up by many other outlets, giving my work so much recognition! The highlight for me was being selected as NASA’s Astronomy Picture of the Day on May 21, 2026.

This work was done during my PhD at Boston University and my time as a predoctoral fellow at CfA. Huge thanks to my collaborators, especially my PI Elizabeth Blanton, for making it possible.

entry.title: Project & Data Manager for the AGEL Survey

link.title: Project & Data Manager for the AGEL Survey

entry.content:
The AGEL Survey

My first post-doc was with the AGEL survey team. During this time, I worked to establish the framework for the AGEL project policies and data management plan, as well as set up the permanent AGEL data archive. This involved creating frameworks and documentation to follow. Examples of two such documents are shown below.

The AGEL Team Roadmap

The Team Roadmap is a document that summarizes:

  • Onboarding new researchers and offboarding leaving team members
  • What resources we have
  • What reserachers were actively involved and their contact info
  • What data products we had on hand and where to find them (which meant wrangling data from a bunch of different scientists…)
  • Some links to tutorials and examples that may help new researchers getting started

The AGEL Data Policies and Management Plan

The Data Policies and Management Plan is a document that summarizes:

  • Best practicies for data handling
  • Instructs users on how to create their Dataverse accounts and upload data to the established AGEL Dataverse archive
  • Creating README files for published data
